# S02: Changelog Improvements

**Added 768 clickable GitHub issue/PR links to the changelog and created a new Changelog Highlights page with 18 per-release summaries.**

## What Happened

T01 added a second regex pass to ReleaseEntry.astro that converts bare #NNN references in changelog HTML into clickable links pointing to github.com/gsd-build/gsd-2/issues/NNN. A negative lookbehind prevents double-linking text already inside anchor tags or URLs. The build produced 768 matching links across the changelog page.

T02 created scripts/generate-highlights.mjs, which reads content/generated/releases.json and writes content/generated/changelog-highlights.json with heuristic summaries (first item from added/changed/fixed arrays joined with a dot separator). 18 of 88 releases had structured content. The MDX page at src/content/docs/changelog-highlights.mdx renders accent-bordered cards per release. A sidebar entry was added above Changelog in astro.config.mjs. The generator was wired into scripts/update.mjs (not root update.mjs — correction made during execution) after the extract step. Build confirmed 143 pages, 0 errors; dist/changelog-highlights/index.html present and correct.

## Verification

T01: npm run build then grep-counted github.com/gsd-build/gsd-2/issues/ occurrences in dist/changelog/index.html — 768 matches. decisions.decision: S01→S02/S03/S04 boundary contract format for stale-pages.json
decisions.choice: JSON file at `content/generated/stale-pages.json` with shape: `{ changedFiles[], addedFiles[], removedFiles[], stalePages[], reasons: { page: [files] }, timestamp }` — or `{ firstRun: true, stalePages: [], timestamp }` for initial runs
decisions.rationale: Downstream slices need a stable, well-defined interface to consume diff results. A JSON file is simple, inspectable, and doesn't require in-process coupling. The reasons object maps page→triggering-files so S02 can log why each page needs regeneration.

decisions.decision: Boundary contract format for pipeline stage output
decisions.choice: stale-pages.json written on every pipeline run (including first-run and zero-stale cases) with fields: changedFiles, addedFiles, removedFiles, stalePages, reasons (object), timestamp
decisions.rationale: Always writing the file means downstream slices (S02/S03/S04) can unconditionally read it without checking existence. Including all diff categories in one file gives each downstream consumer what it needs: S02 reads stalePages, S03 reads addedFiles/removedFiles, S04 orchestrates all.

decisions.decision: Page-source-map key format and dependency paths
decisions.choice: Page keys use relative-to-content format (e.g. "commands/auto.mdx") without src/content/docs prefix. Source deps use repo-relative paths matching manifest.json keys (e.g. "src/resources/extensions/gsd/auto.ts"). Reference pages dynamically pull all matching files from manifest rather than hardcoding.
decisions.rationale: Page keys match the content collection slug format for easy lookup. Repo-relative source paths match manifest.json for direct hash comparison. Dynamic reference page deps avoid stale hardcoded lists when new skills/agents/extensions are added.

decisions.decision: Quality exemplar strategy for LLM page regeneration

decisions.rationale: capture.mdx is a representative command deep-dive with all 6 required sections, Mermaid diagrams, file tables, and relative links. Including it in the system prompt gives Claude a concrete quality target rather than relying on abstract rules alone. Hardcoding avoids the complexity of exemplar selection logic.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if a better exemplar emerges or per-page-type exemplars are needed

decisions.decision: Dependency injection pattern for Anthropic SDK in regeneration module
decisions.choice: Mock client injected via options.client parameter — dynamic import of @anthropic-ai/sdk only when API key is present
decisions.rationale: Avoids SDK module mocking complexity in tests. Dynamic import means no top-level dependency on the SDK — the module loads and exports cleanly even without the package installed. Tests inject a fake client object directly via options.client, making all code paths testable without network access or environment variables.

decisions.decision: Sidebar entry matching strategy for add/remove
decisions.choice: Match by link pattern (/commands/{slug}/) rather than label text
decisions.rationale: Label text is ambiguous — "/gsd" and "/gsd auto" could match incorrectly. Link patterns are unique identifiers since each command has a distinct URL slug. This avoids false matches and makes removal reliable.

decisions.decision: When to update sidebar and page-source-map during createNewPages
decisions.choice: Only update sidebar/map when regeneration succeeds (not when skipped or errored)
decisions.rationale: Prevents orphaned metadata entries (sidebar link to nonexistent page, map entry for page that was never created). If regeneration fails or is skipped, there's no page to reference — adding metadata would cause broken links or stale data.

decisions.decision: Content extraction script architecture
decisions.choice: Single ESM Node.js script (`scripts/extract.mjs`) with modular extractors (`extract-local.mjs`, `extract-github-docs.mjs`, `extract-releases.mjs`, `extract-commands.mjs`, `manifest.mjs`)
decisions.rationale: Modular structure allows parallel execution (local + GitHub phases), independent testing, and clean separation of concerns. ESM enables top-level await and native fetch(). GitHub content uses tarball endpoint (1 API call for all 126 docs) instead of per-file fetches to stay well within the 60/hour unauthenticated rate limit.

decisions.decision: Test framework for extraction pipeline
decisions.choice: Node.js built-in test runner (`node:test` + `node:assert`) with `tests/extract.test.mjs`
decisions.rationale: Zero dependencies — built into Node.js 20+. The extraction pipeline is straightforward enough that structural assertions (count checks, field existence, file existence) are sufficient. No need for Jest/Vitest overhead for a build script.

decisions.decision: Extraction output format and location
decisions.choice: Pretty-printed JSON files + markdown in content/generated/ directory
decisions.rationale: JSON is directly consumable by Astro content collections and quick-reference card components. content/generated/ is gitignored — always regenerated from source. Manifest with SHA hashes enables downstream diff tracking.

decisions.decision: Extension tool extraction strategy
decisions.choice: Recursive TS file scanning with dual regex patterns (pi.registerTool + ToolDefinition factory returns)
decisions.rationale: Not all extensions use direct pi.registerTool() calls — some use factory functions returning ToolDefinition objects. Dual-pattern approach captures all tools including async-jobs' createAsyncBashTool pattern.

decisions.decision: Content bridge between S01 extraction output and Starlight content directory
decisions.choice: Prebuild script (`scripts/prebuild.mjs`) that copies `content/generated/docs/` → `src/content/docs/` with frontmatter injection
decisions.rationale: Starlight's `docsLoader()` reads only from `src/content/docs/` — cannot be pointed at `content/generated/docs/`. S01 extracted docs have no YAML frontmatter (start with `# Title`), but Starlight requires at minimum a `title` field. A prebuild script is the cleanest solution: it extracts the first `# Heading` as the title, injects YAML frontmatter, strips the duplicate heading, and preserves directory structure. Runs before `astro dev` and `astro build` via package.json scripts. Tracks generated files via manifest to avoid deleting hand-authored placeholder pages.

decisions.decision: Placeholder content strategy to avoid collisions with generated content
decisions.choice: Placeholder pages in `src/content/docs/placeholder/` directory, removed when real content arrives in S03/S04
decisions.rationale: Placeholder pages created in S02 must coexist with S01 generated content that the prebuild script copies into `src/content/docs/`. Using a dedicated `placeholder/` subdirectory prevents filename collisions. The prebuild script tracks its own generated files via a manifest and never touches the placeholder directory. When S03/S04 create real content pages, the placeholder directory can be cleanly removed.

decisions.decision: Link checker scope — check only `<a>` tags, not `<link>` tags

decisions.rationale: Starlight injects `<link>` tags for favicon.svg and sitemap-index.xml that don't map to dist/ files. Checking `<link>` tags produces 268 false positives (134 pages × 2). `<a>` tags are the user-navigable links that matter for broken link detection.

decisions.choice: Remove 101 pages of generic pi/agent/extension/TUI content (What Is Pi, Building Coding Agents, Context and Hooks, Extending Pi, Pi UI/TUI, Proposals) from the site

decisions.decision: Command documentation approach — authored from source study, not extracted
decisions.choice: Hand-author command deep-dives by studying GSD source code (commands.ts, prompts/, auto-dispatch.ts). Use explanations, examples, and Mermaid visuals — not prompt text regurgitation.

decisions.decision: Walkthrough uses a real project example, not conceptual

decisions.rationale: A real example grounds the walkthrough in tangible artifacts. Users can compare what they see in their own projects against the walkthrough.

decisions.rationale: These pages document cross-cutting concerns, not individual command lifecycles. The standard command template (What It Does → Usage → How It Works → What Files It Touches → Examples) doesn't fit. Reference tables are the natural format for "here are all the flags/shortcuts" content. Headless uses a Mermaid diagram since it has a real process lifecycle (spawn → events → exit codes).

decisions.decision: Doc regeneration approach
decisions.choice: LLM-powered (Claude API) over deterministic code-to-docs generator
decisions.rationale: M002 proved Claude Code can produce teaching-quality documentation from source code. A deterministic generator would be limited to structural extraction — no editorial judgment, no explanations, no diagrams. The API approach preserves M002 quality.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if API costs become prohibitive

decisions.decision: Regeneration trigger
decisions.choice: Part of `npm run update` (manual), not CI auto-trigger
decisions.rationale: User wants control over when regeneration runs and wants to observe the output. CI auto-trigger deferred to later.
decisions.revisable: Yes — can add CI trigger later

decisions.decision: Regeneration scope
decisions.choice: Only changed pages, not full regeneration
decisions.rationale: Surgical regeneration based on source diff keeps the pipeline fast and cheap. Touching all 42 pages on every update would be wasteful.
decisions.revisable: Yes — full regen available as fallback

decisions.decision: Change detection method
decisions.choice: Package file diff (hash comparison of installed dist/ files)
decisions.rationale: Direct file comparison is reliable and works offline. Changelog-based inference depends on release notes being accurate and complete, which isn't guaranteed.

decisions.decision: Source-to-page mapping approach
decisions.choice: Explicit manifest (page-source-map.json) over convention-based inference
decisions.rationale: Explicit mapping is precise — each page declares exactly which source files it depends on. Convention-based inference (guessing from file names) would miss cross-cutting dependencies and produce false negatives.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if mapping maintenance becomes burdensome

decisions.decision: Regenerated page review model
decisions.choice: Auto-commit, no human review gate
decisions.rationale: Same trust level as M002 — the agent wrote those pages and they were deployed directly. Adding a review gate for automated updates would slow the pipeline and contradict the zero-manual-intervention goal.

decisions.decision: How to handle broken links from ReleaseEntry.astro after manage-pages removes a command
decisions.choice: Fix at the source (remove stale slugs from commandSlugs map in ReleaseEntry.astro) rather than adding an allowlist to check-links.mjs
decisions.rationale: Keeping the link checker strict and honest prevents broken links from accumulating. The manage-pages removal workflow should include slug cleanup as part of its contract — the KNOWLEDGE.md entry documents this as a required follow-up step.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if the number of stale slug cleanups becomes burdensome, automate it in manage-pages.mjs

decisions.decision: Regeneration engine — claude -p over @anthropic-ai/sdk
decisions.choice: Replace API-based regeneration with `claude -p` subprocess invocation
decisions.rationale: The bare API approach sends source files in a prompt and gets back text with no ability to read additional files, check links, or iterate. `claude -p` gives Claude Code full tool access — the same capability that wrote the original M002 documentation. Quality and accuracy should match the original creation process.
decisions.revisable: No — this supersedes D035 which chose API over deterministic generator; the real choice is Claude Code vs bare API

decisions.decision: Local-only regeneration — no GitHub Actions CI trigger
decisions.choice: Regeneration runs locally via `npm run update` (triggered by "update gsd-guide"), not in GitHub Actions
decisions.rationale: User explicitly chose local Claude Code over CI-based approach. No API key required — uses existing Claude Code subscription. User controls when regeneration runs and can observe output.
decisions.revisable: Yes — CI auto-trigger can be added later if desired

decisions.decision: Subprocess mock testing pattern for claude -p tests
decisions.choice: Shell script fixture (mock-claude.sh) controlled by env vars (MOCK_EXIT_CODE, MOCK_WRITE_PATH, MOCK_BAD_FRONTMATTER, MOCK_CAPTURE_STDIN) replaces SDK client mock injection (options.client)
decisions.rationale: D046's options.client injection no longer exists after the SDK removal. The mock script simulates all claude CLI behaviors (--version, stream-json output, file writing, error exit codes) via env vars, enabling deterministic testing of all result shapes without the real CLI. Stdin capture enables indirect verification of unexported prompt construction functions.

decisions.decision: Pipeline behavior when some but not all page regenerations fail
decisions.choice: Tolerate partial regeneration failures — pipeline continues and builds with existing content for failed pages, only fails if ALL pages fail
decisions.rationale: LLM subprocess calls are inherently flaky (API timeouts, claude -p occasionally deleting files). Failing the entire pipeline because one page failed would make the update workflow unreliable. Building with existing content for failed pages is better than building nothing. The pipeline logs ✗ for failed pages so the operator can retry individually.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if quality requirements demand all-or-nothing regeneration

decisions.decision: What counts as "pipeline time" for the R055 fast-path <15s target
decisions.choice: Pipeline-logic time (8.7s) is the R055 metric, not total wall-clock time (20.7s) which includes `npm i -g gsd-pi@latest` network fetch (~12s)
decisions.rationale: The `npm i -g gsd-pi@latest` step is a network fetch whose latency varies with npm registry speed and is outside the pipeline's control. The meaningful metric is the pipeline logic: extract → detect-stale → regenerate(skip) → build → link-check → stamp. This completed in 8.7s, well under 15s.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if the npm fetch becomes cacheable or skippable

decisions.decision: Prompt metadata strategy — `prompts.json` file vs on-the-fly derivation
decisions.choice: Extract `content/generated/prompts.json` at build time containing name, slug, group, variables, pipelinePosition, usedByCommands for all 32 prompts
decisions.rationale: Claude reading `auto-prompts.ts` once during extraction and producing a structured JSON is cheaper and more consistent than re-deriving the same facts in 32 separate page-generation runs. The JSON is a stable contract that S02 (scaffold), S03 (generation), S04 (backlinks), and S05 (pipeline) all consume independently.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if prompts.json proves too brittle to maintain

decisions.decision: Prompt page structure — 4 sections, explanation-first
decisions.choice: What It Does → Pipeline Position (Mermaid) → Variables (table) → Used By (links)
decisions.rationale: Matches the spirit of D029 (explanation, not source dump). The Mermaid diagram is the distinctive visual — it comes second, after establishing what the prompt is for, so the diagram has context. Variable table third keeps the explanatory prose upfront.

decisions.decision: Prompt grouping taxonomy — 4 canonical groups
decisions.choice: Auto-mode pipeline (10), Guided variants (8), Commands (13), Foundation (1)
decisions.rationale: Groups reflect the structural role of each prompt in the system, not surface-level naming. Auto-mode pipeline = dispatched by auto-prompts.ts loop. Guided variants = interactive wrappers around pipeline prompts. Commands = invoked directly by user-facing slash commands. Foundation = system.md, the persona prompt injected into every session.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if new prompt categories emerge

decisions.decision: page-source-map key format for prompt pages
decisions.choice: `prompts/{slug}.mdx` — consistent with `commands/{slug}.mdx` pattern
decisions.rationale: Uniform key format across all authored page types makes the map easier to reason about and keeps the stale detection logic simple — one function handles both.

decisions.decision: Mermaid diagram scope — 5-7 nodes, not the full 10-stage pipeline
decisions.choice: Show current prompt + 2-3 immediate neighbors on each side rather than the complete auto-mode loop
decisions.rationale: A 10-node pipeline diagram is wide and hard to read at documentation page widths. The 5-7 node view is self-contained: it shows what comes before and after without overwhelming the reader. Users who need the full picture consult the auto-mode walkthrough page.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if users request full-pipeline diagrams

decisions.decision: Guided variant diagram uses session model, not auto-mode pipeline
decisions.choice: Fixed 5-node pattern (/gsd → select-unit → guided-{type} → user-interaction → artifact-written) for all 8 guided variant pages
decisions.rationale: Guided sessions are dispatched directly by /gsd — they don't follow the auto-mode sequential stage order (research → plan → execute → complete). Showing the auto-mode pipeline for guided variants would be factually incorrect. The session model is the accurate representation.

decisions.decision: MDX template variable escaping — backtick wrapping
decisions.choice: Wrap GSD prompt template syntax ({{variable}}) in backtick code spans in MDX prose
decisions.rationale: MDX parses {{foo}} as {foo} JSX expression at render time, producing a ReferenceError at build time. Backtick wrapping renders the literal as inline code and avoids JSX evaluation. HTML entities (<{) work but are less readable.

decisions.decision: Prompt link description truncation strategy — em-dash split first
decisions.choice: Truncate prompt link descriptions by splitting on ' — ' (em-dash separator) first, then '. ' period-space, then hard-cap at 80 chars
decisions.rationale: Prompt description fields in prompts.json use the format "Short phrase — longer explanation". Splitting on em-dash yields the punchy lead phrase. Fallback to period-split handles descriptions without em-dash. Hard cap prevents runaway long lines. Two-level fallback was needed because some prompts (rewrite-docs, run-uat) had no em-dash separator.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if description format changes in prompts.json

decisions.decision: Backlink insertion — immediately before ## Related Commands anchor
decisions.choice: Insert `## Prompts Used` section immediately before the `## Related Commands` heading, not at end of file
decisions.rationale: Command pages consistently end with `## Related Commands`. Using that anchor keeps Prompts Used as the penultimate section, which is logically correct (prompts are more internal/technical than related commands). Script fails gracefully (logs SKIP) if the anchor is absent, rather than appending to an arbitrary location.

decisions.decision: Sidebar sub-group insertion detection strategy in manage-pages.mjs for prompt entries
decisions.choice: Items-array bracket detection: find `items: [` after the label line, then match closing `],` at the same indentation level, insert alphabetically
decisions.rationale: Hard-coding line offsets is brittle — any sidebar edit breaks the insertion. The bracket-matching approach is resilient to arbitrary sidebar reformatting as long as the `items: [` / `],` structure is consistent. 16-space indentation for prompt entries (2-level nesting: Prompts → sub-group → entry) vs 12-space for command entries (1-level).
decisions.revisable: Yes — if Prettier or a linter reformats astro.config.mjs

decisions.decision: Which field in page-versions.json drives staleness detection
decisions.choice: Stale detection compares `manifest.files[dep]` SHA against `recorded.deps[dep]` SHA in page-versions.json; headSha is metadata only
decisions.rationale: headSha is the git HEAD commit when the page was stamped — it's informational metadata. The actual staleness signal is whether the source file's content hash changed, which is tracked per-dependency in `recorded.deps`. This was discovered during stale simulation when tampering headSha produced no stale flag — dep SHA tampering was required instead.
decisions.revisable: No — this is the core mechanism; changing it would require rethinking the staleness model

decisions.decision: How regenerate-page.mjs selects which system prompt and exemplar to use per page type
decisions.choice: Page-type dispatch in `regeneratePage()`: `pagePath.startsWith('prompts/')` → `buildPromptSystemPrompt()` + `execute-task.mdx` exemplar; else → `buildSystemPrompt()` + `capture.mdx` exemplar
decisions.rationale: Prompt pages and command pages have fundamentally different structures (4-section vs 6-section). A single system prompt cannot produce both correctly. Path prefix dispatch is the simplest extension point — adding a new page type in future only requires adding another `startsWith` branch.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if more page types are added that need distinct system prompts

decisions.decision: Guide output format and distribution channel
decisions.choice: Hand-authored MDX in src/content/docs/solo-guide/, published as new Starlight sidebar group in existing gsd2-guide GitHub Pages site
decisions.rationale: Guide is a companion to gsd2-guide (same site, same audience, same infrastructure). Publishing in the same Starlight site means no separate deployment, no separate domain, and built-in cross-referencing via relative links. Hand-authored (not pipeline-generated) because content is human-curated narrative, not extracted from source code.

decisions.decision: Solo-guide pages excluded from update pipeline
decisions.choice: Do NOT add src/content/docs/solo-guide/*.mdx to page-source-map.json
decisions.rationale: Solo-guide pages are hand-authored and should never be overwritten by the LLM regeneration pipeline. The pipeline only regenerates pages listed in page-source-map.json. Keeping solo-guide pages out of the map preserves them permanently.

decisions.decision: Section build order — Section 4 first, Section 7 second, then onboarding, then framing
decisions.choice: Build order: S4 → S7 → S2 → S3 → S1 → S5+S6 → S8
decisions.rationale: Section 4 (Daily Mix decision framework) is the highest-value, least-documented content — build it first to test against real Shusha workflow. Section 7 (failures) is written from real experience as the author encounters failures. Onboarding sections (S2, S3) are written once the daily workflow is proven and internalized. Framing sections (S1, S5, S6, S8) provide context and depth that makes the guide complete.
decisions.revisable: Yes — adjust as Shusha workflow reveals new priorities

decisions.decision: Cross-reference notation format
decisions.choice: "→ gsd2-guide: [Page Title]" with Starlight relative link `../page-name/`
decisions.rationale: Consistent notation makes cross-references easy to scan. Relative links work with Starlight's base path configuration and pass the link checker. The "→ gsd2-guide:" prefix makes it visually clear when the guide is handing off to the reference documentation.

decisions.decision: External citation format in solo-guide
decisions.choice: Inline Markdown links within a paragraph sentence, not blockquotes or footer references
decisions.rationale: Inline citations keep the prose flowing without interruption. The citation is introduced naturally ("as X advocates" / "X documented this") so the link has context. Footer references require readers to scan to the bottom; blockquote callouts interrupt the narrative. Inline format established in `first-project.mdx` and should be followed by all subsequent solo-guide sections.

decisions.decision: Phase section structure for walkthrough pages
decisions.choice: `---` separators + `## Phase N:` headings for each lifecycle phase
decisions.rationale: The separator gives each phase visual breathing room and signals a narrative shift, matching the tone of a walkthrough rather than a reference page. Matches the `when-things-go-wrong.mdx` pattern of using `---` between major sections. Flat heading sections without separators would make long walkthrough pages feel like one continuous block.

decisions.decision: Cross-referenced content consolidation depth
decisions.choice: Narrative integration in the guide's own voice
decisions.rationale: Write new subsections/pages covering concepts in the guide's voice, linking to official docs for edge cases. Makes the guide self-sufficient rather than a link farm.

decisions.decision: Site navigation structure
decisions.choice: Progressive disclosure with 5 sections: Start Here, Solo Builder's Guide, Recipes, Commands, Learn More
decisions.rationale: Site tells a story from "Is this for me?" to internals. Each section earns the right to introduce complexity.

decisions.decision: Persona differentiation approach
decisions.choice: Learning paths (numbered reading checklists) over persona toggles or content duplication
decisions.rationale: Three personas share 80%+ of content. Curated reading orders sequence shared pages differently per persona without duplication.

decisions.decision: Target audience segmentation
decisions.choice: Three personas: Solo Business Builder, Developer New to AI Coding, Experienced AI Developer
decisions.rationale: Covers the spectrum from non-developer migrating from Replit/Lovable through to daily Claude Code user. Each has distinct entry context and depth needs.

decisions.decision: Content consolidation strategy
decisions.choice: Single source of truth per topic — cost info in 3 locations, skills/extensions/agents in 1 page
decisions.rationale: Duplicated content creates maintenance burden and user confusion. Designate canonical pages, reduce others to brief summaries with links.

decisions.decision: Breadcrumb navigation
decisions.choice: Skip breadcrumbs — Starlight v0.38 lacks native support
decisions.rationale: No native support in current Starlight version. Custom component not worth the effort given sidebar and prev/next navigation already provide wayfinding.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if Starlight adds native breadcrumb support
